title: Position: Evaluations of AI Moral Reasoning Still Miss Half of the Picture
abstract: arXiv:2608.14566v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent work on evaluating the moral competence of large language models (LLMs) has focused primarily on what we call the moral value problem, i.e., whether model outputs align with human moral values. In contrast, the moral norm problem, i.e., whether models can identify and correctly apply context-sensitive moral norms, remains underexplored. We posit that this imbalance stems from the field's reliance on descriptive ethics frameworks, such as Moral Foundations Theory and Kohlberg's stages of moral development, which emphasize value representation over normative application. We review existing benchmarks and evaluation methods, and show that they cluster heavily around the value problem, while discussion regarding normative ethics remains underrepresented. We identify three crucial gaps: (i) the absence of high-quality ground-truth data for moral norms and their applications, (ii) insufficient evaluation of intermediate reasoning proces

translated_title: 立场：对AI道德推理的评估仍遗漏了半幅图景
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14566v1 公告类型：新 摘要：近期关于大型语言模型（LLMs）道德能力评估的研究主要集中在所谓的道德价值问题上，即模型输出是否符合人类道德价值观。相比之下，道德规范问题，即模型能否识别并正确应用情境相关的道德规范，仍未被充分探索。我们认为，这种不平衡源于该领域依赖描述性伦理框架，如道德基础理论和科尔伯格道德发展阶段理论，这些框架强调价值表征而非规范应用。我们回顾了现有基准和评估方法，并表明它们高度集中于价值问题，而关于规范伦理的讨论仍代表性不足。我们确定了三个关键缺口：（i）缺乏高质量的道德规范及其应用的基准真值数据，（ii）对中间推理过程的评估不足。
tldr: 本文指出当前AI道德推理评估过度聚焦于道德价值问题，而忽视了道德规范问题，并提出了三个关键研究缺口。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that current evaluations of AI moral reasoning overemphasize the moral value problem while neglecting the moral norm problem, and identifies three critical research gaps.
